page.layout: One page of text, single column, with Hebrew and Syriac examples set inline; no margin notes. Page number at the head. Section heading "SECT. V." with subheading "De scheva." above the running text. Catchword "SECT." at the lower right; a signature mark below it.

main_text.p: xum fingularis numeri tertiae perfonae foem. praecedente Camets, ut in ܦܝܫ pes ejus foem. ibi Syri illud punctum quod notat foem. genus, ponunt supra ܥ, praecedente [ܝ] in fingulari, ut ܥܝ ܩ ܝ pes ejus foem.
main_text.head: SECT. V.
De scheva.
main_text.p: Syri scheva non exprimunt, sed intelligunt, cùm fcilicet syllaba pluribus literis constat: quae enim litera vocali caret, intelligitur habere scheva quiescens vel mobile, ut ܒܘܪ bur-ktho, benedictio: ubi ܝ intelligitur habere scheva quiescens, quo trahitur litera ad praecedentia; ܕ vero scheva mobile, quo trahitur ad sequentia.

Eadem vero est Scheva quiescentis & mobilis ratio, quae apud Hebraeos, nisi quòd saepiùs post vocalem longam Scheva fit quiescens apud Syros quam apud Hebraeos, quod usu discendum: hoc tamen observatur, quòd post [ܝ] vocalem, ortam ex quiescentibus media vau, & quietis istius indicem, Scheva fit mobile, ut ܛܘܒܐ tovtho, bona.

page.notes: Hebrew and Syriac words are rendered approximately: the Syriac and Hebrew pointed forms in the scan are small and partly blurred, so the exact vowel points and letters are uncertain and marked here as a whole rather than read letter by letter. "tovtho" and "bur-ktho" are read from the Latin transliteration beside them. Some words are smudged by a stain at "quòd post" and at "pòst" in the line "quòdpòst", which is uncertain. The catchword and signature are read from the foot of the page. Section symbol "§" at the lower left was not transcribed.
